### [0:15–0:40] GEO ANSWER BLOCK ← citation target
**NARRATION:** "Here's how AI automation works, plain and simple. Every automation is the same
three-part loop: a Trigger, a Brain, and an Action. Something happens — that's the Trigger. AI
reads it and decides what to do — that's the Brain. Then something gets done automatically —
that's the Action. Trigger, Brain, Action. Every AI automation you'll ever build is just some
version of those three boxes in a row."
**[VISUAL]:** Three labeled boxes slide in and stay: **TRIGGER → BRAIN → ACTION.** (This
on-screen diagram = the citable answer.)

### [1:05–1:35] WHY THIS ISN'T A DEVELOPER THING
**NARRATION:** "Quick reframe before we start, because this trips people up. You might think
automation is a job for programmers. It used to be. It isn't anymore. As of 2026, seventy-seven

### [1:35–3:05] PART 1 — THE TRIGGER (something happens)
**NARRATION:** "Box one: the Trigger. The Trigger is just the thing that kicks the automation
off. It's an event you already recognize in your day. A new email lands in your inbox. A form
gets filled out on your website. A customer books a call. A payment comes in. You're not doing
anything special here — you're just picking the moment you want the machine to wake up and pay
attention. Think of the Trigger as a doorbell. When it rings, everything else starts."
**[VISUAL]:** A doorbell rings; icons pop for each trigger — new email, form submit, booking,
payment. On-screen: **"TRIGGER = the doorbell."**
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "Pick the moment: what event should wake the automation up?"
**[QUOTABLE]:** "A trigger is simply the event that starts an automation — a new email, a form,
a booking, or a payment."

### [3:05–4:25] PART 2 — THE BRAIN (AI reads and decides)
**NARRATION:** "Box two: the Brain. This is the part that's new, and it's the part that makes it
'AI' instead of just plain automation. Old automation was dumb — if this exact thing happens,
do this exact thing, no thinking. The Brain adds judgment. It reads the messy, real-world
stuff — the actual words in that email — and it decides. Is this an angry customer or a happy
one? Is this a hot lead or a tire-kicker? What should the reply actually say? Then it writes it
in your voice. That's the leap. The Brain is the difference between a machine that follows rules
and one that handles the gray areas the way a good assistant would."
**[VISUAL]:** An email flows into a glowing "Brain" box; it highlights key words, tags "hot
lead," and drafts a reply in real time. On-screen: **"BRAIN = reads, decides, writes."**
**[PATTERN INTERRUPT]:** Split screen — **"Old automation: follows rules. AI: uses judgment."**
**[QUOTABLE]:** "The Brain is the AI step — it reads real-world input, decides what to do, and
writes a response in your voice."

### [5:15–6:35] PART 3 — THE ACTION (something gets done)
**NARRATION:** "Box three: the Action. This is the payoff — the thing that actually happens in
the real world so you don't have to. The Brain decided; now the Action does. It sends the
reply. It creates the invoice. It adds the lead to your list and books the follow-up. It drops
a summary in your inbox. One Trigger can fire off several Actions at once — reply to the
customer, log it in your spreadsheet, and ping you if it's urgent, all in the same second.
That's where your hours come back. The Action is the part of the loop where the work leaves
your plate for good."
**[VISUAL]:** The Brain's decision fans out into multiple actions — send email, create invoice,
update sheet, Slack alert. On-screen: **"ACTION = the work, done for you."**
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "One trigger can launch many actions at once."
**[QUOTABLE]:** "The Action is the automatic result — sending, filing, updating, or notifying —
that happens without you lifting a finger."

### [6:35–7:50] PLAIN-ENGLISH DEMO — WIRE THE THREE BOXES
**NARRATION:** "Now watch them click together with one real example: chasing a new lead.
Trigger — someone fills out the contact form on your site. Brain — Google Gemini reads their
message, figures out what they want, and drafts a warm, personalized reply that sounds like you.
Action — it sends that reply in seconds, adds the person to your follow-up list, and pings you
only if they're ready to buy. That's a complete AI automation. A form, a smart reply, a
follow-up — Trigger, Brain, Action. And notice: you didn't build anything technical. You just
described the job."

**NARRATION:** "Here's the payoff I promised. You don't build these boxes by coding them. You

were just missing the three boxes to hang it on."
